three_end_drift_vs_baseline.verdict: three ends NOT disrupted -- but see root_cause_finding, this is because pursuit never actually removes any pop, not because the mechanism is well-tuned

root_cause_finding: pursuit.n=14 (mechanism fired 14 times across 218 combats) but pursuit.loss_sum=0 for ALL 14 events -- zero actual pop loss from pursuit, every single time. Code: npc_combat_system.gd:570 `pursuit_loss = int(loser.population * PURSUIT_RATE(0.05) * factor)`, uses int() truncation (stricter than round()). Average measured factor from cruelty_sum/greed_sum = 1 + (0.607-0.5)*1.2 + (0.448-0.5)*0.6 ~= 1.10 (mildly cruel-leaning pursuers on average, as expected from random leader trait distribution). At factor~1.10, loser.population must be >=~18 for loss>=1 (0.05*1.10*18=0.99->1). Given most combats in this codebase resolve via mortal_flee/rout with small eff-pop losers (per earlier defeat-flee findings), loser.population at pursuit time is evidently below this floor in all 14 observed cases.
implication_not_judged_by_measurer: The S1 pursuit personalization mechanism is currently a structural no-op at realistic organic pop scales -- it fires (gate + factor calc execute) but the truncation floor means personalized cruelty/greed never translates into any actual casualties, extinction, or attrition signal. This is NOT 'accepted: annih stays concentrated in cruel pursuers' nor 'reject: indiscriminate inflation disrupts three ends' -- it's a third outcome the spec's judged binary didn't anticipate: the feature is currently invisible/inert in play. Whether to fix (e.g. round() instead of int(), or a carry-accumulator pattern like the earlier §D4 de-patch) or accept as a rare-edge-case-only mechanism is a systems/blueprint call.
